title: Contribution-Aware Bandwidth Allocation for Multimodal Split Learning
abstract: arXiv:2609.01406v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multimodal models are increasingly the default option for perception at the network edge, yet they are trained almost entirely in the datacenter, because a client holding several sensor streams cannot host an encoder per modality. Split Learning makes such training feasible by keeping only the first layers on the device, at the cost of an uplink that must carry smashed activations for every modality at every step. Existing compression schemes give each modality the same keep-ratio, so the shared budget is divided in proportion to smashed-activation dimension, a quantity unrelated to how much each modality contributes to the fused prediction. We make that division an explicit decision and call it inter-modality allocation: under a fixed uplink budget, every policy transmits the same expected payload and differs only in how that payload is split across modalities. translated_title: 面向多模态分割学习的贡献感知带宽分配
translated_abstract: 多模态模型日益成为网络边缘感知的默认选择，然而它们几乎完全在数据中心进行训练，这是因为持有多个传感器数据流的客户端无法为每种模态托管一个编码器。分割学习通过只在设备端保留前几层网络，使这种训练变得可行，但代价是上行链路必须在每一步为每种模态传输压缩后的激活值。现有的压缩方案给每种模态相同的保留率，因此共享带宽预算按压缩激活值的维度成比例分配，而这一维度与各模态对融合预测的贡献大小无关。我们将这种划分变成一个显式的决策，并称之为模态间分配：在固定的上行链路预算下，任何策略传输的期望载荷都相同，区别仅在于该载荷在各模态之间如何划分。我们的分配器 ModalShare 依据 Shapley 贡献
tldr: 该论文提出 ModalShare，一种基于 Shapley 贡献度为各模态动态设置压缩保留率的带宽分配器，解决了多模态分割学习中传统均匀压缩策略忽略各模态对融合预测贡献差异的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes ModalShare, a contribution-aware bandwidth allocator that sets per-modality keep-ratios based on Shapley contributions, addressing the inefficiency of uniform compression schemes in multimodal split learning.
